#!/bin/bash
# Windrose native Linux install script
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
# Image to install with is 'ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/installers:debian'
#
# The Steam depot for this app id has no Linux files (Windows only), so the
# native Linux server binaries can only be obtained from the official
# 'windroseserver/windroseserver' Docker image. That image bakes in
# `USER ue_user`, and Wings runs install containers as whatever user the
# image specifies (there is no way to force root via the egg schema), so we
# cannot just `cp` from inside that image - it has no write permission on
# /mnt/server. Instead, pull the image layers directly from the registry
# with this (root) installer and extract them here.
#
# ponytail: assumes no OCI whiteout files under /home/ue_user/app (true as of
# writing - the image only adds files at that path, never removes). If a
# future image version deletes/replaces files via a whiteout, switch to a
# real OCI unpacker (e.g. skopeo copy) instead of this manual layer extract.

set -e

IMAGE="windroseserver/windroseserver"
TAG="latest"
SCRATCH="/mnt/server/_extract"

echo "Authenticating with Docker Hub..."
TOKEN=$(curl -fsSL "https://auth.docker.io/token?service=registry.docker.io&scope=repository:${IMAGE}:pull" | jq -r '.token // empty')
if [ -z "${TOKEN}" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Failed to authenticate with Docker Hub."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Fetching manifest for ${IMAGE}:${TAG}..."
MANIFEST=$(curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -H "Accept: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json" "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/${IMAGE}/manifests/${TAG}")
if [ -z "${MANIFEST}" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Failed to fetch manifest."
    exit 1
fi

# Extract layer digests (jq skips the config digest structurally)
LAYER_DIGESTS=$(echo "${MANIFEST}" | jq -r '.layers[]?.digest')
if [ -z "${LAYER_DIGESTS}" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: No layers found in manifest."
    exit 1
fi
LAYER_COUNT=$(echo "${LAYER_DIGESTS}" | wc -l)
echo "Found ${LAYER_COUNT} layers to download."

mkdir -p "${SCRATCH}"
trap 'rm -rf "${SCRATCH}"' EXIT

for DIGEST in ${LAYER_DIGESTS}; do
    echo "Downloading and extracting layer ${DIGEST}..."
    curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/${IMAGE}/blobs/${DIGEST}" | tar -xz -C "${SCRATCH}"
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Failed to download or extract layer ${DIGEST}."
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Verify the server binary exists before copying
if [ ! -f "${SCRATCH}/home/ue_user/app/R5/Binaries/Linux/WindroseServer-Linux-Shipping" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: WindroseServer-Linux-Shipping binary not found in extracted image."
    exit 1
fi

# Back up mod trios (pak/ucas/utoc) before the vendor copy overwrites Content/Paks.
# Mods live in R5/Content/Paks/ (live) or Mods/ (staging). We preserve complete
# trios only - all three suffixes for a given stem - so UE never sees a dangling file.
MOD_BAK="/tmp/pakmods.bak"
mkdir -p "${MOD_BAK}"
MOD_COUNT=0
for STEM in $(ls /mnt/server/R5/Content/Paks/*_P.pak 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/\/([^/]*_P)\.pak$/\1/' | sort -u); do
    if [ -f "/mnt/server/R5/Content/Paks/${STEM}.pak" ] && [ -f "/mnt/server/R5/Content/Paks/${STEM}.ucas" ] && [ -f "/mnt/server/R5/Content/Paks/${STEM}.utoc" ]; then
        cp -a "/mnt/server/R5/Content/Paks/${STEM}."{pak,ucas,utoc} "${MOD_BAK}/"
        MOD_COUNT=$((MOD_COUNT + 1))
    fi
done
# Also copy complete trios from Mods/ staging if present
if [ -d /mnt/server/Mods ]; then
    for STEM in $(ls /mnt/server/Mods/*_P.pak 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/\/([^/]*_P)\.pak$/\1/' | sort -u); do
        if [ -f "/mnt/server/Mods/${STEM}.pak" ] && [ -f "/mnt/server/Mods/${STEM}.ucas" ] && [ -f "/mnt/server/Mods/${STEM}.utoc" ]; then
            cp -a "/mnt/server/Mods/${STEM}."{pak,ucas,utoc} "${MOD_BAK}/"
            MOD_COUNT=$((MOD_COUNT + 1))
        fi
    done
fi
if [ "${MOD_COUNT}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "Backed up ${MOD_COUNT} mod trio(s)."
fi

# The vendor image always ships R5/ServerDescription.json as an empty stub.
# On a reinstall (= how this egg updates the game) that would silently wipe
# the live server identity and world selection, so preserve it across the copy.
if [ -f /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json ]; then
    cp -a /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json /tmp/ServerDescription.json.bak
fi

cp -a "${SCRATCH}/home/ue_user/app/." /mnt/server/

# Extract the new DeploymentId from the vendor stub before restoring the
# preserved file, so the saved server identity does not carry a stale
# version that would cause client connection failures.
VENDOR_DEPLOYMENT_ID=""
if [ -f /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json ]; then
    VENDOR_DEPLOYMENT_ID=$(jq -r '.DeploymentId // empty' /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json 2>/dev/null) || true
fi

if [ -f /tmp/ServerDescription.json.bak ]; then
    cp -a /tmp/ServerDescription.json.bak /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json
    rm -f /tmp/ServerDescription.json.bak

    if [ -n "${VENDOR_DEPLOYMENT_ID}" ]; then
        jq --arg id "${VENDOR_DEPLOYMENT_ID}" '.DeploymentId = $id' /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json > /tmp/sd.json && mv /tmp/sd.json /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json
        echo "Updated DeploymentId to ${VENDOR_DEPLOYMENT_ID}"
    fi
fi

# Restore mod trios into the new Content/Paks directory
if [ "${MOD_COUNT}" -gt 0 ]; then
    cp -a "${MOD_BAK}/"* "/mnt/server/R5/Content/Paks/"
    echo "Restored ${MOD_COUNT} mod trio(s) to Content/Paks."
fi
rm -rf "${MOD_BAK}"

# Strip debug symbols and debug binary to save ~2.1GB of disk space
echo "Stripping debug files to save disk space..."
DEBUG_COUNT=$(ls /mnt/server/R5/Binaries/Linux/*.debug 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
SYM_COUNT=$(ls /mnt/server/R5/Binaries/Linux/*.sym 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
rm -f /mnt/server/R5/Binaries/Linux/*.debug
rm -f /mnt/server/R5/Binaries/Linux/*.sym
if [ "${DEBUG_COUNT}" -gt 0 ] || [ "${SYM_COUNT}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "Removed ${DEBUG_COUNT} .debug and ${SYM_COUNT} .sym files."
fi

# Ensure the server binary is executable
chmod +x /mnt/server/R5/Binaries/Linux/WindroseServer-Linux-Shipping

echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"
